info.title: SeoulMarkets: Korea, Japan, Taiwan and UAE Company Filings Data
info.description: Financials, valuation, 5% ownership filings and convertible bonds for 7,600+ listed companies in Korea, Japan, Taiwan and the UAE. Taken from regulator filings, returned in English JSON. Free tier, no card.

get.summary: Filed annual financial statements for Korean listed companies, as filed to DART
get.description: One row per company per fiscal year (fnlttSinglAcntAll, annual report). `measured:false` means DART had no annual statement on file for that company and year — those rows carry nulls, never zeros. `basis` says CFS (consolidated) or OFS (separate-only). This is what companies filed, not our estimate. `?ticker=` returns every year on file for one company; otherwise a filtered, paginated list.

get.summary: PER, PBR, ROE and debt-to-equity for listed Korean companies
get.description: One row per listed company. Consolidated (CFS) financials are used when available, otherwise separate (OFS) — the `basis` field says which. PER is null when net income is not positive; PBR and ROE are null when total equity is not positive. No sector averages are computed. `?ticker=` returns one company by its 6-digit KRX short code; otherwise a filtered, paginated list.

get.summary: Latest annual accounts of Tokyo-listed companies, as filed with EDINET
get.description: One row per company: the most recent annual securities report filed with the Financial Services Agency of Japan (EDINET, Public Data License 1.0). Assets, equity, revenue, operating and net profit, shares, BPS, EPS and the filed PER. `price_jpy` and `market_cap_jpy` are fiscal-year-end values implied by the filed PER x EPS, not live quotes. `market` is null for every row because the EDINET code list does not state the market segment. Empty cells are null, never zero.

get.summary: Latest quarterly accounts of TWSE-listed companies, from the TWSE OpenAPI
get.description: One row per company: the most recent quarter published through the Taiwan Stock Exchange OpenAPI (Open Government Data License, Taiwan, version 1.0). Income-statement figures are cumulative from the start of the year, not a single quarter. Amounts are in New Taiwan dollars (units). Includes closing price with its date, PER, PBR and dividend yield as published by the exchange. Empty cells are null, never zero.

get.summary: Revenue, net profit, EPS and (where reconciled) balance sheet for ADX and DFM filers
get.description: ADX rows come from the exchange's own AI-extracted summary; DFM rows are parsed directly from the filed PDF. Not an audit — we did not re-check the filed figures. `total_assets_aed` is null unless `balance_sheet_reconciled:true` (assets = liabilities + equity checks out) or `liabilities_derived:true` (liabilities backed out from assets − equity, flagged, never hidden). `unit_hint` must be read together with the figures — some filers report in thousands.

get.description: DART ownership disclosures for Korean listed companies, as two filing types selected by `kind`. `kind=filings` (default) is substantial-shareholding (5%+) reports (majorstock) — one row per filing, with `holder_name` exactly as filed. `kind=executives` is officer/major-shareholder ownership status (elestock) — one row per filing, with `person_name` exactly as filed and `is_registered_officer` null when the filer is a major shareholder rather than an officer. Names are never romanized or translated; `reason_raw_ko` (filings only) is the original Korean filing reason, not summarized. Not a full float table — only holders required to file. `?filing_id=` returns one filing by its exact DART receipt number; otherwise a filtered, paginated list.

get.summary: Convertible bond, bond-with-warrant and exchangeable bond filings
get.description: DART filings for CB, BW and EB — coupon, maturity, strike and refixing-floor terms as filed. One row per filing. `refix_floor_price_krw` is null for EB by design (exchangeable bonds have no refixing floor) — `refix_floor_note` carries the filed reason when one exists; both null means we could not measure it. Not a dilution forecast or a signal — terms as filed only. `?filing_id=` returns one filing by its exact DART receipt number; otherwise a filtered, paginated list.

get.summary: Workforce filings for listed Korean companies, by gender
get.description: Headcount, tenure and pay by gender, as filed with the Financial Supervisory Service, joined to KRX closing price. One row per company. Ratio fields (`women_share_ratio`, `tenure_ratio_women_to_men`, `pay_ratio_women_to_men`) are raw 0-1 figures, not percentages. `pay_ratio_women_to_men` is null when a filing did not carry the figure — `pay_ratio_withheld_reason` distinguishes a filed reason (not applicable) from an unmeasured gap (also null). This is not a discrimination claim, a benchmark or a company ranking — see the coverage `not_this` notes. `?ticker=` returns one company by its exact KRX code; otherwise a filtered, paginated list.

get.description:
Every target price and investment rating issued by Korean brokerages that we have
collected: 2,610 records across 20 years, normalised to English.

Three normalisations matter, and each is exposed as an added field beside the raw one:

- `brokerEntity` — a stable id per legal entity. Korean brokerages rename often, and one
  firm appears under up to four Korean names in the archive. Group by this, not by `broker`.
- `ratingNormalised` — 22 source spellings (Korean, English, mixed case, one typo, one
  truncation) folded into 8 levels. `Outperform` is deliberately kept below `Buy`;
  in Korea it is one notch down, not a synonym.
- `subjectEn` — official English company name. A company sets its own spelling
  (SK hynix, NCSOFT, AMOREPACIFIC), so this cannot be derived by rule.

Fields that are unknown are `null`. We never fill a gap with a plausible-looking value.
Report text and PDFs are not collected, so nothing copyrighted is redistributed —
these are facts about what was published, not the publications.

parameters.name: broker
parameters.description: Korean name, English name, or entity id. All three resolve to the same firm, and a match returns every historical name of that entity — querying "Mirae Asset" also returns its Daewoo Securities-era reports.

parameters.name: subject
parameters.description: Company covered by the report. Korean name as filed.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: Earliest report date, YYYY-MM-DD. Note the archive is sparse before 2014 — see GET /meta.

parameters.name: rating
parameters.description: Filter on the normalised level, not the broker wording. Unknown values return 400 with the valid list.

parameters.name: stance
parameters.description: Coarser than rating. Useful context: 94.1% of rated reports are positive and 0.16% negative — 89 negative records in 20 years.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Newest first.

200.description: Matching reports. A filter that matches nothing is 200 with count 0 — not an error.

brokerEntity.description: Stable across renames. Group by this.

brokerType.description: Explains a null target price: credit-rating and IR bodies publish analysis without one (4,164 records).

subjectEn.description: null when not yet in the dictionary.

targetPrice.description: KRW. null means no target was published — not zero.

score.description: Our ordering for aggregation. Not a number the broker assigned.

detailFetched.description: false means the target price was never fetched, not that none exists.

source.description: Every response names where its facts come from.

400.description: Unknown rating or stance. The hint lists the valid values.
